_why: Headron Bench, first freebench run: an external, unassisted (blind) run of free model routes over this repository's task families. Only lanes the source scored are here; its N/A lanes are counted in `excluded` and carry no numbers.
run: one overnight run; the contract version it ran against was not reported
raw_records: not in this repository: this file holds the run's reported summary, so no number here is re-derivable from a record
arm: blind: no Headron contract in any prompt. These numbers rank model capability; Headron's effect was not measured
error_policy: errored records scored 0 inside each mean (INFERRED: the source counts answers as records minus errors, and its means fit only that). A score is therefore not a score over answers; errors and records are stored so it can be recomputed

excluded.na_why: N/A in the source (a partial or all-error run): freeroute-backend and -vision on main; freeroute-small and -deep on advanced and context; kilo-dots and freeroute-small, -deep and -judge on enterprise. The host went to idle sleep at 02:15 ET and took the router and tunnel down, so these are transport failures, not capability results
excluded.not_run: six Kaggle egress lanes and the local Qwen kernel, freeroute-offline and freeroute-train, and freeroute-judge on advanced and context: no records

enterprise.fixes: dedupe, duration and window solved and ratelimit 0.0 in every scored lane, so the fixes do not separate lanes; the 11 route-label tasks decide this round

void.FIX_ratelimit: its plant passed its own test, so an unchanged file would have scored 1.0; the universal 0.0 has an UNCERTAIN cause. Plant and test fixed after this run
void.FIX_dedupe: its plant (list(set(...))) passed its own test on some hash seeds, so a solve could be free. Plant made deterministic after this run

context.note: every lane scores the same: the round carries no ranking signal, and its prompts are short, so it is not a long-context test

reading: chain lanes (freeroute-*) are router chains: resolved_model is the model the router served that night, from its log. Five chain lanes resolved to one model and scored 0.861 to 0.877, which is this run's measured noise
one run per lane: a gap smaller than that noise is not an ordering, and no lane is named a winner here
